_meta.indication: VIMPAT (lacosamide) tablets are indicated as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients with epilepsy aged 17 years and older; injection is indicated as adjunctive therapy when oral administration is temporarily not feasible

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center (US and Europe), double-blind, parallel group trial of lacosamide 200, 400, or 600 mg/day vs placebo given Q12H, with an 8-week baseline phase
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with partial-onset seizures on 1 or 2 concomitant AEDs with at least 4 seizures/4 weeks during baseline
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction from baseline in 4-week seizure frequency during the maintenance phase (ANCOVA on log-transformed seizure frequency)
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reduction in seizure frequency vs placebo: 200 mg/day -14.8% (p=0.14), 400 mg/day -27.9% (p=0.003), 600 mg/day -21.5% (p=0.026)

pivotal_trials.design: Same design as Study 667 but with only 3 groups (placebo, 400, and 600 mg/day), performed entirely in the US
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with partial-onset seizures on concomitant AEDs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction from baseline in 4-week seizure frequency during the maintenance phase
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reduction in seizure frequency vs placebo: 400 mg/day -21.2% (p=0.011), 600 mg/day -24.8% (p=0.009)

pivotal_trials.design: Similar design to the other two studies but with 3 arms (placebo, 200, and 400 mg/day), performed in Europe and Australia with a 4-week titration phase
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with partial-onset seizures on concomitant AEDs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction from baseline in 4-week seizure frequency during the maintenance phase
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reduction in seizure frequency vs placebo: 200 mg/day -13.6% (p=0.05), 400 mg/day -27.3% (p=0.027)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and greater than placebo) are diplopia, headache, dizziness, and nausea. In the AE table (VIMPAT Total N=944 vs placebo N=364): dizziness 31% vs 8%, headache 13% vs 9%, nausea 11% vs 4%, diplopia 11% vs 2%. Discontinuation for AEs was 8% at 200 mg/day and 17% at 400 mg/day (the recommended doses), 29% at 600 mg/day (above the recommended range), vs 5% placebo
target_moa: The precise mechanism is not fully elucidated; lacosamide selectively enhances slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels, stabilizing hyperexcitable neuronal membranes and inhibiting repetitive neuronal firing

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved

description.text: Added use of Vimpat as monotherapy (conversion to and initial) for partial-onset seizures in patients age 17 years and older

citations.quote: The use of Vimpat as monotherapy (conversion to and initial) in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients with epilepsy age 17 years and older.

description.text: Expanded the treatment of partial-onset seizures to include pediatric patients 4 years of age and older (previously limited to older patients)

citations.quote: VIMPAT is indicated for the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 4 years of age and older.

description.text: Added adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures in pediatric patients 4 to <17 years of age

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications report the results of SP0969, a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of lacosamide as adjunctive therapy in subjects with epilepsy \ge 4 years to <17 years of age with uncontrolled partial-onset seizures. The revised labeling contained in these supplements provides for the addition of new or worsening seizures to the Adverse Reactions; Postmarketing Experience section, based on a safety signal assessment.

description.text: Expanded to add adjunctive therapy for primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures and to lower the age for both indications to patients 4 years of age and older

citations.quote:
- Treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 4 years of age and older (1.1)
- Adjunctive therapy in the treatment of primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in patients 4 years of age and older (1.2)

description.text: Expanded to oral and intravenous monotherapy and adjunctive therapy for partial onset seizures in pediatric patients 1 month to <4 years of age

citations.quote: The use of lacosamide for oral and intravenous monotherapy and adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial onset seizure patients \ge 1 month to <4 years of age. Increase of in-use shelf-life for oral solution from 7-weeks to 6-months to support proposed indication in partial onset seizure patients \ge 1 month to <4 years of age.

description.text: Added alternate initial loading dose for initiating lacosamide in pediatric partial onset seizure patients ≥1 month to <17 years and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizure patients ≥4 to <17 years

citations.quote: The use of alternate initial dosing (loading dose) for initiation of lacosamide treatment in partial onset seizure patients \ge 1 month to <17 years of age and in primary generalized tonic-clonic seizure patients \ge 4 to <17 years, across all formulations.

summary.text: Traditional approval of a new molecular entity for adjunctive treatment of partial seizures in adults, based on three adequate and well-controlled trials; a REMS with Medication Guide was required, and FDA recommended the product be scheduled under the Controlled Substances Act

citations.quote: The sponsor has submitted adequate evidence of safety and substantial evidence of effectiveness for the use of lacosamide oral tablets as adjunctive treatment for partial seizures in adults with epilepsy.
Pursuant to 21 CFR Part 208, FDA has determined that Vimpat (lacosamide) poses a serious and significant public health concern requiring the distribution of a Medication Guide.
We have recommended that this product be scheduled under the Controlled Substances Act.

requirement.text: A nonclinical study in rats to examine the effects of lacosamide on brain development during the prenatal and early postnatal periods using more sensitive techniques than the standard pre- and postnatal development study

citations.quote: A nonclinical study in rats to examine the effects of Vimpat (lacosamide) on brain development during the prenatal and early postnatal periods using more sensitive techniques for assessing central nervous system structure and function than were employed in the standard pre- and postnatal development study.

requirement.text: In vitro data to determine which enzymes may be involved in the metabolism of lacosamide in addition to CYP2C19

citations.quote: *In vitro* data to determine which enzymes may be involved in the metabolism of Vimpat (lacosamide) in addition to CYP2C19.
